$comment: Source of truth for which tests back each capability claim in PARITY_MATRIX.md.
scripts/check-parity.mjs verifies that every cited file exists and that the
matrix's yes/— columns match these citations exactly. An earlier revision of
the matrix claimed integration coverage for three capabilities that had none;
this file makes that class of claim checkable rather than a matter of trust.
Cite a file only when it genuinely exercises the capability.
A capability may also carry a `clauses` inventory: one entry per specification
clause, each with the real section reference and evidence naming a *test*
rather than a file. scripts/lib/clause-gate.mjs refuses a PASS whose mandatory
clauses are not evidenced. PARITY_MATRIX.md, under 'Clause-level evidence',
explains the six statuses and which of them block a PASS. Do not widen an
existing citation to cover a clause it does not test: that is the exact move
the gate exists to catch, and tests/unit/clause-gate.test.ts proves it does.

Closed in Wave 14. `BrowserAdapter.moveTab` existed and was called by nothing; a tool now wraps it, which is where a capability is declared in this architecture — schema, risk, site scope and registration. The reported index is read back from the browser because `chrome.tabs.move` clamps instead of failing.

clauses.note: Re-audited in Wave 16 and found half-blank. The runtime's terminal path reported to the lifecycle observer; `TaskManager.fail` did not, and three failures end there — a provider that could not be resolved, a resume whose provider no longer matches, and a failed planning turn. None of those raised the notification, wrote the task.completed audit record, or released the task's staged files. `fail` now reports like every other ending.

Closed in Wave 16. The clause had no producer: an account only ever became `disconnected` during cloud-metadata restore, a backend path, and a rejected credential surfaced as a task error. There are now two producers, both in the worker's task lifecycle layer and neither in any adapter. At resolve time — which runs at the start of every task, resume and scheduled run — a provider that rejects its stored credentials marks the account `disconnected` and notifies. Mid-run, a credential revoked during a task reaches the lifecycle observer as a terminal AUTH_EXPIRED, which the provider layer treats as terminal because a rejected key is rejected on every retry; a rate limit or a 503 is deliberately not treated as a disconnect. The notification carries the build's own provider id and never the account's display name, endpoint or key.

clauses.note: Closed in Wave 17, and precise about what it establishes. §14 lists nine minimum checks; eight were performed and the ninth was absent from the report entirely, while the context window was copied from the advertised model table. There is now a real probe: the model must carry a substantial prompt and the provider must report its own token count for it. That is a measured **floor**, not the window, and the check's own text says so — the window is still reported as this build's advertised figure and is labelled as not measured. Finding the ceiling would mean billing the user for a diagnostic, and reading it from provider model metadata is not uniformly available. The floor catches what the table cannot: an account tier whose usable context is far below the number published for the model.

clauses.requirement: On detection, stop and recover or ask.
clauses.note: Resolved in Wave 17 by an explicit product decision, recorded rather than assumed. §59's "stop and recover/ask" is a disjunction, and this product answers it by asking: the run halts, the reason is separately identifiable as LOOP_DETECTED rather than a generic failure, the user-facing message says the task stopped and names the choice, the error is marked recoverable, the panel shows Retry for any finished task, and §53's task-failed notification fires. Automatic recovery is deliberately NOT attempted, and that is the divergence: §58's recovery ladder is given as an "Example:" rather than a requirement, and retrying a call the detector has just proved unproductive would re-enter the loop the check exists to break.
